notes: Overall: rc.5 passes every gate (eval-1.md) and keeps the chrome from rc.4: 16px pixel face, night ground, cream type, 4px windows with darker interiors, dither rules, gold marker, hue bars and bullets, block meters and the checkered grass strip (blog/home-desktop-dark.png, dashboard/home-desktop-dark.png, settings/settings-profile-desktop-dark.png vs reference/screenshots/p1-desktop-light.png). Scene composition has clearly improved: there is now a focal group, three graded ridge layers, night-toned walls and a clear hero Window. The banners and strips still fall short of the reference banners in scale and rhythm. Arithmetic: 4, 4, 4, 4, 4, 4, 3 averages 3.86, below the 4.0 bar. No score is below 3. Signature is the only dimension below 4.

rc.4 issues, one by one. (a) Catalogue row, no focal group: PARTLY FIXED. Each app now has a focal group taller and more detailed than its neighbours: the clock tower and brick block (blog/drawings/posts-shipping-a-design-system-d1.png), two shop cabinets (commerce/drawings/home-d1.png), a dish with two racks (dashboard/drawings/home-d1.png), a workshop shed with a transformer (settings/drawings/settings-profile-d1.png). On a squint the focal group reads first. But the supporting props are still evenly strung across the whole width on one baseline, with gaps of about 45 to 55 units each (blog/drawings/about-d1.png: 10 supporting props at near-even spacing; dashboard/drawings/home-d1.png: 9 props at near-even spacing). (b) One flat ridge: FIXED. Haze, far and near layers are graded and checkered (blog/drawings/posts-shipping-a-design-system-d1.png, light; blog/posts-shipping-a-design-system-desktop-dark.png, dark), comparable to reference/illustrations/p2-i2.png. (c) Strip numbers: MOSTLY FIXED. The commerce strip has about 8 props plus poles, with upright cabinets and an awning stall carrying a person (commerce/drawings/home-d1.png). The settings strip has 7 props. (d) Night tones: FIXED. Dark walls are mixed toward the sky and only windows, signs and the moon glow (blog/home-desktop-dark.png brick block and clock tower; commerce/products-canvas-field-tote-desktop-dark.png), as in reference/illustrations/p1-i1.png. (e) Hero Window over props: FIXED. Under the Window there is only sky, ridges and ground, and the first prop starts at about x 608 at 1440px (blog/drawings/home-d1.png; blog/home-desktop-dark.png). (f) Vignettes as icons: FIXED. They are now small scenes with sky bands, a ridge, ground and a focal pair: a mailbox and lamp (blog/state-search-empty-desktop-dark.png), a rack, crate and lamp (dashboard/state-empty-filter-desktop-dark.png), a stall and lamp (commerce/cart-mobile-dark.png). (g) Duplicates in settings: NOT FIXED. See signature. (h) Ground sprite height: FIXED within tolerance. The blog mailbox, commerce cabinet and settings reel are each about 36 to 44px. (i) Product detail columns: FIXED. The picture window ends about 150px above the purchase column plus Details (commerce/products-canvas-field-tote-desktop-dark.png).

Regressions against rc.4. (1) The blog hero thinned out. rc.4's hero (showcase/runs/night-cartridge/0.1.0-rc.4/blog/20261014-221142/drawings/home-d1.png) had a dense street with window grids, a mailbox, a van and a cat. rc.5 (blog/drawings/home-d1.png) has 5 props and 2 lamps over 1440px. Sparseness is fidelity to the reference hero (reference/illustrations/p1-i1.png: one cabin, a tree, a figure, a pole). What is missing is what makes the reference's sparse hero work: its foreground is a landform (a rising hill, a path, grass tufts and a fence line). rc.5's near ground is a flat dark band with about ten dashes, about 75px of empty field across the full width in dark (blog/home-desktop-dark.png y 380-455). (2) The supporting props shrank. In rc.4 the banner buildings were about 28 to 32 units tall with window grids. In rc.5 the supporting props are 12 to 16 units in a 128-unit banner (blog/drawings/about-d1.png) and carry two or three window pixels each. The banner is now mostly landscape with small props at the bottom. Scored once, under signature.

Signature (3). Placement passes: hero on the blog home, banners on the article and about pages, strips on the store, product, cart, dashboard and settings screens, vignettes on empty states, a prose figure (blog/drawings/posts-shipping-a-design-system-d2.png) and the ground strip everywhere. Motion keyframes are present (shots.json: drift, twinkle, blink, bob, swap, sparkle, rare). The drift frames step the cloud in whole units (blog/motion/motion-m1.png, settings/motion/motion-m1.png). Reduced motion passes. The remaining gaps against the reference: (a) Scale. In the reference banner the focal subject and its trees fill about 40 to 50% of the banner height and cross the ridge layers (reference/illustrations/p2-i2.png, p2-i3.png). Here the focal group is 28 to 36 of 128 units, about 25%. The supporting props are about 12% and none cross the haze layer (blog/drawings/posts-shipping-a-design-system-d1.png, blog/drawings/about-d1.png). At 1x in dark, the commerce and dashboard strips read as specks in a thin band (commerce/home-desktop-dark.png, dashboard/home-desktop-dark.png), where the reference's figure and trees read at a glance. The recipe's 28–40-unit focal range for a 128-unit banner causes this, so it is a spec gap. (b) Rhythm. The supporting props are spaced almost evenly from edge to edge (blog/drawings/about-d1.png, dashboard/drawings/team-d1.png), where the reference groups its trees into clusters with open snowfield between them (p2-i2.png). The recipe's 'gaps 4–60 units' allows even spacing at 50. (c) Duplicates, an agent mistake the spec already forbids (step 4 'copies differ by 4+ units' and Verification). Settings repeats an identical workbench at x≈410 and x≈925 and an identical blue switch panel at x≈523 and x≈795 (settings/drawings/settings-profile-d1.png, settings-billing-d1.png). The agent report claims the recipe's numbers but lists no variant differences (settings/agent-report.md). (d) Hero foreground, as in regression (1) (blog/drawings/home-d1.png vs reference/illustrations/p1-i1.png). Under 'Screens differ by crop, a prop or which lights are on', the dashboard home, team and project strips show the same props in the same places (dashboard/drawings/home-d1.png, team-d1.png, projects-apollo-migration-d1.png). The spec allows a lights-only change, so this is not deducted.

Cross-app consistency (4): one family in all four apps, light and dark. Shared: the chrome, type, meters, markers, ground strip, scene layering and night toning. The world split (post office, market, server yard, workshop) holds. The blog's banners are wide landscapes with 128-unit scenes, while the other three run 48-unit strips. The spec asks for this split, so it is not a drift.

Hierarchy (4): every screen leads with the scene window and its h1, then section titles on dither rules, then content (commerce/home-desktop-dark.png, settings/settings-profile-desktop-dark.png), as in reference/screenshots/p1-desktop-light.png. Gold appears only on the page commit (Read the featured post, Add to cart, Place order, Save changes, Confirm change). The solid cyan chart bars are still the heaviest mass on the dashboard home (dashboard/home-desktop-dark.png). This is unchanged from rc.4 and minor.

Spacing (4): the 4px scale and the 64px section rhythm hold, and the product detail balance is fixed. Small issue: on settings, the form windows are capped at about 600px while the strip window and the Active sessions window span about 960px in the same column. This leaves a 350px void beside each form (settings/settings-security-desktop-light.png, settings/settings-profile-desktop-dark.png). It reads as two grid widths, but the agent states it as a deliberate decision, so it is not deducted to 3.

Component states (4): designed throughout. Gold 4px focus frame on inputs (blog/state-search-empty-desktop-dark.png, commerce/state-checkout-errors-desktop-dark.png). Danger frames with pixel '!' messages. A disabled ◀ stepper. A dialog with a title bar, a framed close button, a framed Cancel and a gold Confirm (settings/state-plan-dialog-desktop-dark.png). Empty states with a vignette, a sentence and a framed '▶ Clear filters'. A current-device row marker on Security (settings/settings-security-desktop-light.png). Not a 5: loading and pending states are never captured (harness gap, not penalized).
Polish (4): no default-browser leftovers. Radius is 0, borders are 2/4px, and the hard shadow appears only on gold buttons and the dialog. Scene defects are scored only under signature.

Not penalized (known harness gaps): the sticky header captured mid-page in state shots (blog/state-search-empty-desktop-dark.png, dashboard/state-empty-filter-desktop-dark.png); the dialog scrim ending at about 900px in the full-page capture (settings/state-plan-dialog-desktop-dark.png); no pending request; motion frames for the blog and settings only. The light theme is derived: the blue sky and mint ridges in the light crops are accepted as the day palette.
promptFixes: Banner scale (signature, spec gap): in Pixel stage step 4, change the banner and hero focal group from '28–40 units' to '48–64 units (about 40–50% of the scene height), at least one sprite crossing the haze ridge line', and supporting props from '12–24' to '20–36, at least two tall vertical props (a tree, a tower, a mast) crossing the far ridge'. Keep the strip numbers. Add to step 8: 'in place at 1440px, the focal group is at least 100px tall in a banner; if props sit only in the bottom third, scale up.' Evidence: blog/drawings/posts-shipping-a-design-system-d1.png and blog/drawings/about-d1.png (focal group about 25% of the height, supporting props about 12%, nothing crossing the haze) vs reference/illustrations/p2-i2.png and p2-i3.png (figure and trees about 40–50% of the height, crossing every ridge layer).

Clusters, not even spacing (signature, spec gap): in step 4 replace 'gaps 4–60 units' with 'group supporting props into 2 or 3 clusters of 2–4 props (gaps inside a cluster 2–10 units) separated by open ground of 60–160 units; no three consecutive gaps within 10 units of each other.' Add to Verification: 'list the gaps between props left to right.' Evidence: blog/drawings/about-d1.png and dashboard/drawings/team-d1.png (props at near-even gaps of about 45–55 units edge to edge) vs reference/illustrations/p2-i2.png (tree clusters with open snowfield between).

Hero foreground as a landform (signature, spec gap): in the Hero placement add: 'the near ground is a landform, not a flat band: a rise or slope of 8–16 units under the focal group, a path or track of 2-unit steps toward it, and 25+ hand-placed tuft or stone runs in the near layer.' Count them in step 7 under the hero's 120+. Evidence: blog/drawings/home-d1.png and blog/home-desktop-dark.png (flat near band about 75px tall with about ten dashes) vs reference/illustrations/p1-i1.png (hill with path, fence and tufts).

No identical copies (signature, an agent mistake the spec already forbids): move 'two identical props in one scene' into the Never list. Make Verification a required table in the agent report: 'variant | x positions | what differs (4+ units)'. A scene with a repeated variant and no table fails. Evidence: settings/drawings/settings-profile-d1.png (identical workbenches at x≈410 and x≈925, identical switch panels at x≈523 and x≈795); settings/agent-report.md has no variant list.
